# 2 Samuel Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 172r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** And-heard [the]-son of-Sha'ul that Avner died in-Chevron, and-dropped his-hands [raphū yadav], and-all Yisra'el were-dismayed.

**4:2** And-two men, commanders of-raiding-bands, were to-[the]-son of-Sha'ul; [the]-name of-the-one [was] Ba'anah, and-[the]-name of-the-second [was] Rekhav, sons of-Rimmon the-Be'erotite, from-[the]-sons of-Binyamin; for also Be'erot was-reckoned upon Binyamin.

**4:3** And-fled the-Be'erotites to-Gittayim, and-they-are sojourners there until this day.

**4:4** And-to-Yehonatan son of-Sha'ul [was] a-son, smitten of-feet [nekheh raglayim]. A-son of-five years he-was when-came the-report of-Sha'ul and-Yehonatan from-Yizre'el, and-lifted-him-up his-nurse and-fled. And-it-was in-her-hurrying to-flee, and-he-fell and-became-lame [vayyippaseach]. And-his-name [was] Mefivoshet.

**4:5** And-went [the]-sons of-Rimmon the-Be'erotite, Rekhav and-Ba'anah, and-came at-[the]-heat of-the-day to [the]-house of-Ish-Boshet, and-he [was]-lying-down [the]-lying-down of-noon.

**4:6** And-they-came there to [the]-midst of-the-house, taking wheat, and-struck-him to-the-belly [chomesh]; and-Rekhav and-Ba'anah his-brother escaped.

**4:7** And-they-came [to] the-house, and-he [was]-lying upon his-bed in-[the]-room of-his-lying-down, and-they-struck-him and-killed-him and-removed his-head. And-they-took his-head and-went [by the]-way of-the-Aravah all the-night.

**4:8** And-they-brought [the]-head of-Ish-Boshet to David to-Chevron, and-said to the-king, "Behold, [the]-head of-Ish-Boshet son of-Sha'ul your-enemy, who sought your-life [nephesh]; and-gave YHWH to-my-lord the-king vengeance this-day from-Sha'ul and-from-his-seed."

**4:9** And-answered David Rekhav and-Ba'anah his-brother, [the]-sons of-Rimmon the-Be'erotite, and-said to-them, "[As]-lives YHWH who-redeemed my-soul [nephesh] from-all distress —

**4:10** the-one-who-told me, saying, 'Behold, Sha'ul is-dead,' and-he was in-his-[own]-eyes as-a-bearer of-good-news [mevasseir] — I-seized-him and-killed-him in-Tsiqlag, which [was] to-give-him [as]-the-reward of-his-news [besoratō].

**4:11** How-much-more [af ki] when wicked men have-killed a-righteous man upon his-bed in-his-house — shall-I-not now seek his-blood from-your-hand and-remove-you from the-earth?"

**4:12** And-commanded David the-youths, and-they-killed-them and-cut-off their-hands and-their-feet and-hung [them] by the-pool in-Chevron. And-[the]-head of-Ish-Boshet they-took and-buried in-[the]-tomb of-Avner in-Chevron.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — raphū yadav:** Literally "his hands dropped" — an idiom for losing courage/strength. The narrator shows Ish-bosheth's psychological collapse upon hearing of his protector's death.

**v.4 — Mefivoshet:** This parenthetical note about Jonathan's lame son is narratively significant — it establishes that no able-bodied Saulide heir remains. The name may derive from *mephi-boshet* ("from the mouth of shame") or be a deliberate corruption of an original *Merib-ba'al* ("contender of Baal," cf. 1 Chr 8:34).

**v.6 — MT textual issue:** The MT of v.6 is problematic. The Hebrew reads literally "coming there to the midst of the house, taking wheat" — suggesting they used the pretext of collecting wheat to gain entry. The LXX (Vaticanus) has a different reading: "the doorkeeper of the house had been cleaning wheat and she dozed off." The MT is followed here as the primary text.

**v.10 — mevasseir/besoratō:** Bitter irony — the Amalekite *thought* he was bringing good news (*besorah*) and expected a reward. David gave him death as his "reward." The same irony now recurs with Rechab and Baanah.

*— EMET*
